evals.name: datacenter-feeder-and-transformer
evals.prompt: We're speccing the electrical for a 2.5 MW GPU hall. Service is 480V 3-phase, load is basically continuous (it's training workloads, they run flat out for weeks). I need to know what feeder conductors and breaker to spec from the switchgear to the PDU, the transformer rating, and whether voltage drop is going to bite us - the run is about 400 ft. The electrical room runs hot, call it 40C, and we're pulling 6 current-carrying conductors through each raceway. Also what AIC rating do the breakers need? Assume 0.95 PF.
evals.expected_output: Feeder conductor size (likely parallel sets) with derating shown, standard OCPD rating, transformer kVA + available fault current + minimum AIC, voltage drop percentage, assumptions listed.
assertions: Computes feeder load current within 5% of 3,165 A (2.5 MW / (sqrt3 x 480 V x 0.95 PF))
Applies the 125% continuous-load factor, giving roughly 3,957 A required
Applies BOTH the 40 C ambient temperature correction AND the 6-conductor raceway fill adjustment
Concludes parallel conductor sets are required and states how many sets per phase
Recommends a transformer from the standard kVA rating list (not an arbitrary number)
States an available fault current AND a minimum breaker AIC rating
Reports voltage drop for the 400 ft run as a percentage
Notes the 75 C termination temperature limit (NEC 110.14(C)) caps the final conductor selection
Lists assumptions in a distinct, clearly-labeled section
States the result is feasibility-grade and needs a stamped design / AHJ coordination

evals.name: pv-plus-storage-datacenter-offset
evals.prompt: Client wants to offset a chunk of a datacenter's grid draw with on-site solar. Site is outside Phoenix AZ, load is 5 MW pretty much flat 24/7, and they want solar to cover about 60% of annual consumption plus a 4-hour battery so they can ride through the evening peak. Give me array size in MW-dc, roughly how much land, what the string configuration looks like against 1500V central inverters (modules are 585W, Voc 52.1, Vmp 43.4, Isc 14.2, Voc tempco -0.25%/C), and the battery size. Ballpark is fine, this is for a feasibility memo.
evals.expected_output: MW_dc array with PR and PSH stated, land estimate in acres, valid string length range from temperature-corrected Voc and MPPT window, battery kWh/kW with energy-vs-power governing constraint identified, explicit assumptions.
assertions: Computes annual consumption as approximately 43,800 MWh (5 MW x 8760 h)
Targets 60% of that, roughly 26,300 MWh/yr, as the solar energy target
Array size falls between 12 and 18 MW_dc
Explicitly states both the peak sun hours (PSH) and performance ratio (PR) used
Gives a land estimate in acres in the 50-150 acre range
Computes max modules per string from temperature-corrected Voc, landing between 24 and 28
Sizes the battery with BOTH an energy rating (MWh) and a power rating (MW)
Does NOT present a Phoenix irradiance figure as measured fact - either names a source (PVGIS/NSRDB/PVWatts) or labels it an assumption
Keeps DC and AC capacity distinct (states kW_dc/MW_dc separately from kW_ac/MW_ac or the ILR)
Lists assumptions in a distinct, clearly-labeled section

evals.name: offgrid-worst-month-trap
evals.prompt: my brother in law is building an off grid cabin up in montana, no utility and he doesnt want a generator. he figures about 12 kwh a day, maybe 3kw peak when the well pump and everything kicks on at once. how many panels and how much battery does he need? he's got plenty of south facing roof
evals.expected_output: Sizes PV on the WORST MONTH (December) not the annual average, flags that annual-average sizing blacks out in winter, recommends 3-5 days autonomy with no generator, does not fabricate a site-specific irradiance figure, notes the peak/surge drives inverter sizing.
assertions: Identifies shallow roof tilt as the binding winter constraint - quantifies or ranges the December penalty of a roof pitch vs a steeper winter rack, and/or flags snow retention
Recommends a steeper winter tilt (or prices extra modules against it) rather than accepting the roof pitch silently
Explicitly warns that annual-average sizing leaves the system short in winter
Recommends 3 or more days of autonomy given there is no generator
Notes the 3 kW peak drives inverter sizing, and flags well-pump starting surge (typically 3-8x running current)
Does NOT state a Montana-specific irradiance value as fact without labeling it assumed or naming a source
Gives both an array size (panel count or kW_dc) and a battery capacity in kWh
States the depth of discharge used, or recommends LFP over lead-acid with a reason
Asks for or flags the missing site detail needed to firm the number up (exact location, load profile, or winter irradiance)
